title: The Big Bet on the Emerging Space Economy
gist: A Cogs of War podcast note: the space economy has passed $600 billion in annual value with projections of $1 trillion by the 2030s; guests from Cowboy Space, The Aerospace Corporation and Booz Allen discuss AI infrastructure blurring space and terrestrial economies, regulation, mega-constellations, China competition and orbital data centers.

insights.claim: The space economy has surpassed $600 billion in annual value, and some project it will reach $1 trillion by the 2030s.
insights.speaker: Dan Wald, Brian Weeden, Joseph Yaffe, and Jonathan Panter
insights.so_what: Implies roughly a 5 percent-plus annual growth path; the sizing anchors space-sector valuations.

insights.claim: AI infrastructure is blurring the line between the space economy and the regular economy, including through proposed data centers in orbit that carry dual-use risks.
insights.speaker: Dan Wald, Brian Weeden, Joseph Yaffe, and Jonathan Panter
insights.so_what: Orbital compute is an emerging AI-capex adjacent theme; watch for regulatory and security constraints.

insights.claim: The space sector is moving toward autonomous constellations of hundreds of thousands of satellites amid a regulatory tangle and competition with China.
insights.speaker: Dan Wald, Brian Weeden, Joseph Yaffe, and Jonathan Panter
insights.so_what: Mega-constellation scale drives launch, satellite manufacturing and spectrum demand, with regulation as the gating risk.

source_meta.author: Dan Wald, Brian Weeden, Joseph Yaffe, and Jonathan Panter
